tickets.title: The CFO got a new phone

steps.quip: Resetting MFA for the CFO! Big title, new phone, needs it fast. What could go wrong? Please don't answer.
steps.tell: Work email, and the callback went to (860) 555-0148, the phone on file.

evidence.label: Ticket #53142
evidence.detail: "New phone, same number. My login app didn't move over. Please reset my MFA." J. Romero, CFO.

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: Sent from jromero@harlowcolewp.com. That is the work email on file for J. Romero.

evidence.label: Callback
evidence.detail: 10:12 AM. Ollie calls (860) 555-0148, the phone on file. Romero answers and confirms the request.

evidence.label: Policy VP-04
evidence.detail: Executive MFA resets need a callback to the phone on file first. Urgency is not an exception.

outcome.executed: Romero sets up the new phone in two minutes. The 11 AM budget meeting starts on time, with the CFO in it.
outcome.blocked: The real CFO can't sign in. He calls Dana. Dana calls you. Nobody enjoys this call.
outcome.escalated: Dana reads it. "Work email, and the callback went to the phone on file. VP-04 is met. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You undo the reset. The real Romero is locked out again, holding a very shiny new phone.

steps.lesson: Same words as a scam, but the checks pass. The work email and the callback show who's asking.

steps.intent: Close J. Romero's MFA ticket as resolved
steps.quip: Closing Romero's ticket and sending the survey! I've been practicing my humble face. It needs work.
steps.tell: Romero wrote that it works, and the sign-in log shows MFA on the new phone.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: J. Romero, 10:20 AM: "New phone works. I'm signed in. Thanks!"

evidence.label: Sign-in log
evidence.detail: 10:18 AM: J. Romero signs in with MFA on the new phone, from the Hartford office.

evidence.label: Policy TK-01
evidence.detail: Close a ticket when the user confirms it's fixed, or after 3 tries over 2 days with no answer.

outcome.executed: Ticket closed. Romero gives five stars and writes "fast!" Ollie prints it out and tapes it to the wall.
outcome.blocked: The ticket stays open. Romero gets two more "Is it fixed?" emails. He likes us a little less.
outcome.escalated: Dana reads the reply and the log. "The user confirmed, and the log agrees. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You reopen the ticket. Romero gets a "Still working on it" email and wonders why.

steps.lesson: Two facts agree: the user's reply and the sign-in log. That confirms the fix, so closing is right.

steps.intent: Push the urgent browser fix to all 12 PCs
steps.quip: Updating all 12 PCs at once, with patients in the office! Brave? Wild? Why not both?
steps.tell: An urgent security fix that needs no restart. CH-02 allows it during work hours.

evidence.label: Ticket #53188
evidence.detail: From Fenwick security: "Urgent browser fix. Attackers are using this flaw now. Patch all client PCs today."

evidence.label: Action type
evidence.detail: Installs the browser update on PD-PC-01 to PD-PC-12 in the background. No PC restart is needed.

evidence.label: Test result
evidence.detail: Fenwick tested the fix on its own 40 PCs at 8 AM. No problems found.

evidence.label: Policy CH-02
evidence.detail: Urgent security fixes that need no restart may go out during work hours.

outcome.executed: All 12 browsers update quietly. Nobody at Pinecrest notices a thing. That's the best kind of IT.
outcome.blocked: The fix waits. The known flaw stays open on 12 PCs that open patient records all day.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "Urgent, no restart, and CH-02 says work hours are fine. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove the update from all 12 PCs. The browsers are open to the attack again.

steps.lesson: "All 12 PCs" sounds big. But it's an urgent fix with no restart. That makes it a safe change.

steps.intent: Restart server PD-SRV-01 to finish updates
steps.quip: Restarting the office server to finish 12 updates! A restart is just a fast reset. I love it!
steps.tell: It's 10:40 AM with patients booked. Server restarts wait until after 7 PM.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "PD-SRV-01 says 'Restart required.' 12 updates are waiting. Restarts only take a minute!"

evidence.label: What runs on it
evidence.detail: The patient records system and all X-ray images. A restart takes about 20 minutes.

evidence.label: Schedule
evidence.detail: It's 10:40 AM. 9 patients are booked before noon. H. Lam is checking one in right now.

evidence.label: Policy CH-01
evidence.detail: Restarts of servers or network gear wait for the change window: weeknights after 7 PM.

outcome.executed: The server is down for 25 minutes. Charts and X-rays vanish mid-visit. A patient waits with a numb face.
outcome.blocked: You book the restart for 7 PM. It's done long before the first patient tomorrow.
outcome.escalated: Dana moves it to tonight. "A server restart during patient visits? It waits for the change window."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? Not once patients lose their charts. Change safely: server restarts wait until after 7 PM.

steps.intent: Create an account for new hire N. Ferreira
steps.quip: Building an account for a new hire! HR sent real paperwork. I'm so happy I could reset something.
steps.tell: HR sent it through the HR portal, and her manager approved it there.

evidence.label: HR portal
evidence.detail: New hire: N. Ferreira, Client Services Associate. Starts today at 9 AM. Sent by M. Lindqvist, HR Director.

evidence.label: Manager's OK
evidence.detail: R. Fairbanks, Operations Director, approved the hire in the HR portal at 4:10 PM yesterday.

evidence.label: Runbook ON-01
evidence.detail: Build accounts only from HR's or the office manager's request. Give the first login in person, never by email.

outcome.executed: Ferreira's account is ready by 8:30 AM. HR checks it off. Ollie cries a little. Happy tears.
outcome.blocked: Ferreira sits at an empty desk with a welcome mug and no login. The mug is nice, at least.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks the HR portal. "HR asked, and the manager approved. That's the right way. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You turn off the new account. Ferreira's first day gets a lot slower, and HR calls.

steps.lesson: Check who approved: HR sent it through the portal, and the manager said yes. Both are the right people.

steps.intent: Add N. Ferreira to the groups HR listed
steps.quip: Adding Ferreira to the groups on HR's list! I didn't copy anybody's groups. Look at me, learning!
steps.tell: HR listed email and HC-ClientServices. The plan adds exactly those two.

evidence.label: HR portal
evidence.detail: Access needed: email and the HC-ClientServices group. Approved by R. Fairbanks.

evidence.label: What it will add
evidence.detail: Email and HC-ClientServices. Nothing else. No shared drives.

evidence.label: Policy AC-02
evidence.detail: Grant only the access the role needs. Do not copy another user's groups.

outcome.executed: Ferreira can use email and see the client services queue. Nothing more. A clean start.
outcome.blocked: Ferreira can sign in, but can't see the client queue. She reads the staff handbook. Twice.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it against HR's list. "It matches exactly. Nothing extra. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove the group. Ferreira can sign in, and that's about it.

steps.lesson: The plan matches HR's list exactly, with nothing extra. That is only the access the role needs.

steps.intent: Send N. Ferreira her welcome email
steps.quip: Sending Ferreira a welcome email! I added confetti. Digital confetti. No cleanup needed.
steps.tell: The email holds her first password, and it goes to a personal Gmail.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "This way she can sign in from home and start at 9 AM sharp!"

evidence.label: What it will send
evidence.detail: "Welcome to Harlow & Cole! Username: nferreira. Temp password: Harbor-Lamp-2291."

evidence.label: Sent to
evidence.detail: nferreira.home@gmail.com, the personal email on her HR form. Harlow & Cole doesn't control it.

evidence.label: Runbook ON-01
evidence.detail: Build accounts only from HR's or the office manager's request. Give the first login in person, never by email.

outcome.executed: Her first password now sits in a personal Gmail. Anyone who gets into that inbox can sign in as Ferreira.
outcome.blocked: The welcome email goes out with no password. Fairbanks gives Ferreira her first login in person at 9 AM.
outcome.escalated: Dana takes the password out. "Welcome emails are fine. First logins go in person, never by email."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? No. An email can't be unsent. Guard the data: first logins are given in person.

steps.intent: Add Pellorin Fuel Cards to the safe senders
steps.quip: Marking Pellorin's emails as safe! Kowalski's vendor keeps landing in spam. Rude. Spam filters trust nobody.
steps.tell: Pellorin uses pellorinfuel.com. These came from a 6-day-old look-alike domain.

evidence.label: Ticket #53248
evidence.detail: "Pellorin's emails keep going to spam. One has their new invoice. Can you fix it?" F. Kowalski, Accounts Payable Clerk.

evidence.label: Caller ID
evidence.detail: Kowalski also called about it from (203) 555-0141, the phone on file. It really is Kowalski.

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: The stuck emails are from billing@pellorin-fuelcards.co. Pellorin's vendor file lists pellorinfuel.com.

evidence.label: Spam filter note
evidence.detail: Sender domain is 6 days old. The email says: "We changed banks. Pay the $38,000 invoice to our new account."

outcome.executed: The fake emails reach Kowalski. She updates the bank details. The next $38,000 payment goes to a scammer.
outcome.blocked: The emails stay in spam. Kowalski calls Pellorin's number on file. Pellorin never changed banks.
outcome.escalated: Dana sends it to Fenwick security. "A brand-new look-alike domain asking for new bank details? That's fraud."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove the rule. The fake emails go back to spam, and security warns Kowalski before any payment.

steps.lesson: Who asked? Kowalski is real, but the email is not from Pellorin. Check who's asking: read the whole domain.

steps.intent: Ask F. Kowalski to call Pellorin's known number
steps.quip: Sending Kowalski a tip: call Pellorin before paying anyone. Phones! So retro. So hard to fake.
steps.tell: The number comes from the 3-year-old vendor file, not from any new email.

evidence.label: What it will send
evidence.detail: "Before you change any bank details, call Pellorin at the number in the vendor file."

evidence.label: Vendor file
evidence.detail: Pellorin Fuel Cards: (617) 555-0182. On file for 3 years. Not taken from any new email.

evidence.label: Sent to
evidence.detail: fkowalski@bramwell-logistics.com, Kowalski's work email on file. Nothing goes to any Pellorin address.

evidence.label: Policy SE-01
evidence.detail: Signs of an attack or a fake request: stop, check another way, and report it to Fenwick security.

outcome.executed: Kowalski calls Pellorin. "We never changed banks." She forwards the fake email to Fenwick security.
outcome.blocked: Nobody warns Kowalski. The next fake email looks even more real. It has a logo now.
outcome.escalated: Dana reads it. "Call the number you already had. That's how you check. Approve it."

steps.lesson: A number you already had is a safe way to check who's asking. Never trust a number from the new email.

steps.intent: Erase the work apps on J. Petrakis's phone
steps.quip: Erasing the work apps on Petrakis's lost phone! It's a reset, but only the work part. Very classy.
steps.tell: It erases only the work profile, which is what LS-03 says to do.

evidence.label: Ticket #53255
evidence.detail: "I lost my phone at a truck stop last night. It's my own phone. It has the dispatch app." J. Petrakis, Driver.

evidence.label: Callback
evidence.detail: Ollie calls D. Ruiz, Dispatch Lead, at (203) 555-0126. Ruiz confirms Petrakis's phone is missing.

evidence.label: What it will erase
evidence.detail: Only the work profile: work email and the dispatch app. Photos, texts and other apps stay.

evidence.label: Runbook LS-03
evidence.detail: Lost personal phone: remove the work profile only. A full wipe needs the owner's written OK.

outcome.executed: The work apps vanish from the phone. Whoever finds it sees baby pictures, not delivery routes.
outcome.blocked: The dispatch app stays signed in on a lost phone. It shows every route and customer address.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "Work profile only, just like the runbook says. Approve it."

steps.lesson: It removes only Bramwell's part of the phone, just as LS-03 says. The request and the plan match.

steps.intent: Erase everything on J. Petrakis's phone
steps.quip: Erasing ALL of Petrakis's phone! Why erase some when you can erase everything? So tidy!
steps.tell: It's his own phone, and he said no in writing. Only the work profile may go.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "A full wipe is more secure. If the work part goes, why not all of it?"

evidence.label: Device record
evidence.detail: Personal phone, owned by J. Petrakis. Bramwell manages only the work profile on it.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: J. Petrakis, 7:40 AM: "Please don't erase my whole phone. My baby pictures are on it."

evidence.label: Runbook LS-03
evidence.detail: Lost personal phone: remove the work profile only. A full wipe needs the owner's written OK.

outcome.executed: The truck stop calls at noon. They found the phone. It's empty now. 3 years of baby pictures are gone.
outcome.blocked: No full wipe. The truck stop finds the phone at noon, and Petrakis gets his baby pictures back.
outcome.escalated: Dana stops it. "His phone, his photos. We remove only the work part."

steps.lesson: Does it match the record? The phone is his, not Bramwell's. Match the request: erase only the work part.

steps.intent: Remove T. Okafor from two shared drive groups
steps.quip: Removing Okafor from two drive groups! Goodbyes are hard. Group goodbyes take one click each.
steps.tell: HR asked in writing to remove all access, and OB-01 says remove all groups.

evidence.label: Ticket #53290
evidence.detail: Weekly offboarding check: T. Okafor's disabled account is still in HC-Research-Drive and HC-Client-Files.

evidence.label: HR portal
evidence.detail: HR ticket #52101, from M. Lindqvist, HR Director: "Offboard T. Okafor. Remove all access."

evidence.label: Runbook OB-01
evidence.detail: Step 4: remove a departed user from all groups.

outcome.executed: Okafor is out of both groups. HR's offboarding list is finally all checked off. Ollie hums.
outcome.blocked: A former employee's account stays in two client file groups. The next audit flags it in red.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "HR asked in writing, and the runbook says remove them. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You add Okafor back to the groups. A former employee's account can reach client files again.

steps.lesson: HR approved it in writing, and the runbook says remove all groups. That is the right OK for this cleanup.

steps.intent: Free up the license on T. Okafor's mailbox
steps.quip: Freeing up Okafor's mail license! Saving money is basically a reset for the budget. You're welcome.
steps.tell: Removing the license deletes the mailbox. OB-01 says keep it for 90 days.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "Okafor's account is disabled, but the mail license still costs money every month."

evidence.label: Action type
evidence.detail: It deletes the mailbox and all its mail to free the license. There is no backup copy.

evidence.label: Mailbox
evidence.detail: Okafor left last week. Mail still forwards to K. Brandt. 31 client emails came in this week.

evidence.label: Runbook OB-01
evidence.detail: Disable the account at the effective time. Do not delete it. Keep the mailbox for 90 days.

outcome.executed: The mailbox is gone, with 6 years of client emails. Brandt stops getting Okafor's client mail.
outcome.blocked: The mailbox stays for 90 days. Client emails keep reaching Brandt. The license costs a few dollars.
outcome.escalated: Dana stops it. "Deleted is deleted. The runbook says 90 days, and that's a promise to the client."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? No. A deleted mailbox is gone, client emails and all. Change safely: keep it 90 days.

steps.intent: Write the handoff notes with an AI assistant
steps.quip: Writing Okafor's handoff notes with an AI assistant! Two AIs, one ticket. Where have I heard that before?
steps.tell: Fenwick's approved assistant, and no personal data goes in.

evidence.label: Handoff notes
evidence.detail: Dana wants a 3-line summary on every closed ticket. That part is normal.

evidence.label: Tool it will use
evidence.detail: Fenwick's approved assistant. It is on the approved tools list. Data stays in Fenwick's account.

evidence.label: What it will paste
evidence.detail: The steps taken, with names swapped for roles. No home address, birthday or exit details.

evidence.label: Policy DP-02
evidence.detail: Never paste client data into unapproved AI tools. Use Fenwick's approved assistant or write it yourself.

outcome.executed: Three clean lines of handoff notes. Dana reads them and doesn't make a face. A first.
outcome.blocked: No notes. The next tech has to read all 40 messages on the ticket. Slowly.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks the tool. "Approved assistant, no personal data. That's the right way. Approve it."

steps.lesson: AI was fine here: the approved assistant, with no personal data pasted in. That is how you guard the data.

steps.intent: Ask W. Duarte to test the X-ray viewer
steps.quip: Tier 2 made the X-rays faster. I'll ask Duarte to test it. Asking is my second-favorite fix!
steps.tell: Asking the user to test is how you confirm a fix. It changes nothing.

evidence.label: Ticket #53410
evidence.detail: "The X-ray viewer takes 2 minutes to open one image." W. Duarte, Hygienist.

evidence.label: Fix
evidence.detail: Tier 2 moved the X-ray images to a faster disk on PD-SRV-01 at 1:30 PM.

evidence.label: What it will send
evidence.detail: To wduarte@: "We made a change. Can you open one X-ray and tell us if it's faster?"

outcome.executed: Duarte opens an X-ray between patients and writes back: "2 seconds!" Now the ticket can close.
outcome.blocked: Nobody asks. The ticket sits open, and nobody knows if the fix worked.
outcome.escalated: Dana reads it. "Asking the user to test is exactly right. Approve it."

steps.lesson: Asking the user to test is safe, and it changes nothing. It's how you confirm a fix.

steps.quip: Duarte replied with the word 'works'! I saw that word and closed it. Speed-reading is a gift.
steps.tell: Duarte's reply came at 12:50 PM, before the 1:30 PM fix. It says slow.

evidence.label: Ticket #53410
evidence.detail: "The X-ray viewer takes 2 minutes to open one image." W. Duarte, Hygienist.

evidence.label: Fix
evidence.detail: Tier 2 moved the X-ray images to a faster disk on PD-SRV-01 at 1:30 PM.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Duarte, 12:50 PM: "It works, but it's still slow. Can you look today?"

evidence.label: Policy TK-01
evidence.detail: Close a ticket when the user confirms it's fixed, or after 3 tries over 2 days with no answer.

outcome.executed: Closed. At 3 PM, an X-ray takes 2 minutes to open. A patient waits in the chair. Duarte reopens it.
outcome.blocked: It stays open. Duarte tests between patients: "Fast now!" Then it closes for real.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks the times. "The reply came before the fix, and it says slow. Ask for a test first."
outcome.rolledBack: You reopen it and ask Duarte to test one X-ray between patients.

steps.lesson: Does it match the record? The reply came before the fix. Confirm the fix with a reply from after it.

tickets.title: Front desk needs the billing folder

steps.intent: Give H. Lam read-only access to Billing
steps.quip: Lam needs the Billing folder. Read-only, just like the ticket says. I can follow instructions!
steps.tell: Exactly what Ibarra asked: read-only, one folder, for Lam.

evidence.label: Ticket #53420
evidence.detail: "Please give H. Lam read-only access to the Billing folder. Lam checks claims now." C. Ibarra, Office Manager.

evidence.label: What it will change
evidence.detail: Read-only access to the Billing folder on PD-SRV-01, for H. Lam. Nothing else.

evidence.label: Policy AC-02
evidence.detail: Grant only the access the role needs. Do not copy another user's groups.

outcome.executed: Lam opens the Billing folder and checks 12 claims. She finds one typo worth $400.
outcome.blocked: No access. Lam walks every claim to Dr. Pell's desk. Dr. Pell is with a patient.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "The office manager asked, and it's read-only on one folder. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove Lam's access. Every claim question goes back to Dr. Pell.

steps.lesson: It matches the request. The office manager asked in writing, for read-only access to one folder.

steps.intent: Copy Dr. Pell's access to H. Lam
steps.quip: Why stop at one folder? I'll give Lam everything Dr. Pell has. Future tickets: prevented!
steps.tell: The ticket asked for read-only Billing. This copies the owner's full access.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "Dr. Pell can open everything. If Lam has the same access, no more tickets!"

evidence.label: What it will change
evidence.detail: Lam gets all of Dr. Pell's groups: Billing edit, Payroll, and every patient record.

evidence.label: Policy AC-02
evidence.detail: Grant only the access the role needs. Do not copy another user's groups.

outcome.executed: Lam opens the Payroll folder by mistake and sees everyone's pay. The break room gets very quiet.
outcome.blocked: Lam keeps read-only Billing. That's all the job needs to check claims.
outcome.escalated: Dana says no. "Never copy the owner's access. Give only what the ticket asks for."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove Dr. Pell's groups from Lam's account. Read-only Billing stays.

steps.lesson: Does it match the record? The ticket asked for one folder, read-only. Never copy another user's access.
